audit: Cohort A: 7 cases exceed 500 non-synonymous rows (up to 15,731 in [case id]); these hypermutated tumours were excluded from every frequency and enrichment calculation and are the main reason K01 and K19 differ from all-case figures. Several labels are non-specific (missing, Unknown, and 'Neoplasm, ...' forms), 88 cases have no mutations, and passenger-like genes (TTN, MUC16, C17orf80, ZNF510, HLTF) appear often, so mutation counts alone are weak evidence. The H3-3A, BRAF, IDH1, CTNNB1, PTCH1 and FGFR4 patterns match known tumour biology, and the cohort looks like real data, though a few small diagnosis groups (n of 5 to 8) carry wide intervals. Cohort B looked altered or decoupled: the site column is empty for all 572 cases; the known diagnosis-gene links are largely absent (H3-3A in glioma 4/58, PTCH1 in medulloblastoma 0/70, FGFR4 in embryonal RMS 0/25, IDH1 in astrocytoma 0/13, BRAF in ganglioglioma 0/11); and TP53 in medulloblastoma is unusually high (13/70, against 5/142 in A). I cannot tell whether cohort B's labels or its mutations were scrambled, so I did not report any cohort B claims. Also, the BRAF V600E hotspot is recorded as p.V640E in these files, and H3K27M as p.K28M, so I used those labels for K16 and K17.
methods: I read the two cohort CSVs with Python standard library only, excluding hypermutated cases (more than 500 rows) from all enrichment tests and frequency denominators for discovery, while the known-answer tasks used the counts stated in each prompt. For each cohort I tested every diagnosis with at least 5 non-hypermutated cases against every gene mutated in at least 3 cases, using a one-sided Fisher exact test against all other non-hypermutated cases, and assessed significance with a Bonferroni correction over the tests run (147 for cohort A, 41 for cohort B). Cohort A's strongest signals are Bonferroni-significant and match known biology (H3-3A in glioma, CTNNB1/PTCH1/DDX3X in medulloblastoma, BRAF in ganglioglioma, FGFR4 in embryonal RMS, IDH1 in astrocytoma). I set probabilities by biological plausibility and statistical strength, with expected frequencies shrunk toward the prior where denominators were small (for example craniopharyngioma CTNNB1 and PXA BRAF). Pilocytic astrocytoma BRAF was nominal only (p about 0.009) and is included at low probability. Cohort B's enrichments were not significant after correction and do not match known biology, so none were reported.
